result.body: The first time Somto said she needed a quiet place, Didi didn’t even take her serious. “Quiet place?” Didi laughed, almost spilling her drink. “In this Nigeria? Where exactly you wan see am?” ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXCLKmmKGnurKRAnURNQmpPjcoLSyjVVtfjM7Fr2gUReu/1776327580517.jpg) Somto just shook her head resting her chin on her palm. "I’m serious Didi. Everywhere is too noisy. My head isn’t resting.” They were sitting outside a food joint. A generator was humming loudly behind them ,Plates were clanking. People were arguing over change. “Madam your balance isn’t complete!” “Check it well!” Didi leaned closer. "So what’s happening? You have never been like this before.” Somto sighed. "Nothing really…. Everything at the same time, School, people, noise, my own thoughts… it is like my brain won’t calm down.” Didi looked at her for a second then smirked. "You have started overthinking right? You just need small rest.” “I need more than rest my dear " Somto said quietly. "I need silence.” Two days later Somto was packing a small bag. Didi sat on the bed watching her like she was about to do something illegal “So you are actually doing this thing?" she asked. “Yes " Somto replied, folding her clothes neatly. "I just want to go somewhere quiet for a bit.” “Alone?” “Yes.” Didi frowned. "This isn’t a heartbreak thing is it?” Somto laughed. "Not everything is a man problem okay.” “Okay " Didi said, raising her hands. "Just make sure you are safe and call me.” “I will.” The journey was longer than Somto expected, When she finally got there she noticed the difference immediately. No horns. No shouting. No generator noise. Just… calm. She stepped down slowly looking around like she wasn’t sure it was real. “Wow…" she whispered. "So places like this still exist?” She checked into a lodge, It wasn’t fancy, It was neat and quiet , The woman at the desk smiled warmly, "You are welcome, you came alone?” “Yes.” “You will enjoy it here , it is very peaceful.” Somto smiled, "That’s what I came for.” That evening she went for a walk, the road was almost empty, a few people were passing by quietly, trees lined the sides, the breeze felt soft against her skin, she found a bench nearby and sat down. For once she did not reach for her phone, she just sat there breathing and listening to nothing. Somehow that nothing felt like everything she needed. “You like it here?” Somto turned quickly. A girl stood beside the bench holding a nylon bag, "Sorry " the girl said with a smile, "I didn’t mean to scare you.” “It’s okay " Somto replied, "I just wasn’t expecting anyone.” The girl nodded, "This place is always like this, quiet, calm, some people don’t like it, but love it.” Somto smiled. "Same here, that is why I came.” The girl sat down beside her, "I’m Didi.” Somto blinked, then laughed, "Didi?” “Why are you laughing?" she asked, raising an eyebrow. “My friend’s name is Didi too.” “Ah, what a coincidence " she grinned. "So what’s your name?” “Somto.” They sat quietly for a while, It didn’t feel awkward at all. After a minutes Didi spoke again. “You know that sometimes it is not the noise that is the problem?” Somto looked at her, "What do you mean?” “Even if everywhere is quiet , if your mind isn’t calm you won’t feel at peace.” Somto nodded slowly, "Hmmm that is true.” “So what are you running from?" Didi asked gently. Somto exhaled, "Honestly I don’t even know, i just feel overwhelmed, It is like everything is just too much.” Didi smiled softly, " It will be like that sometimes, you don’t always need to run, sometimes you just need to sit with yourself.” Somto leaned back thinking about it. “Hmm… I have never really tried that.” “Well " Didi said, pointing her hand around. "This is a good place to start.” That night Somto lay on her bed staring at the ceiling. No noise. No distractions. Just quiet. For the first time in a long while her mind wasn’t racing, It wasn’t completely silent, It felt lighter. “Maybe I needed this " she whispered. The morning her phone rang, It was her friend Didi. “Madam traveler " her friend’s voice came through. "How are you? did you find your quiet place?” Somto smiled. “I think I have or at least I’m getting there.” “So you won’t come back again?" her friend teased. Somto laughed. "I will come back, I have learned something.” “Something how?” “That quiet place I was looking for… it’s not just a location. It’s something you create inside yourself too.” There was a silence. “Wow " her friend said finally. "You have changed o” Somto laughed softly. “Maybe a little.” That day she returned to the same bench. Same breeze. Same silence. This time she closed her eyes. Instead of running from her thoughts… she let them settle. For the first time, in a long while… Everything felt calm. Waterproofing in Toronto is an essential service for homeowners dealing with the region’s challenging climate. With frequent rainfall, snowmelt, and fluctuating temperatures, properties in Toronto are especially vulnerable to water intrusion. Basements, in particular, are at high risk due to hydrostatic pressure building up around foundations. Without proper waterproofing, moisture can seep through cracks, leading to structural damage, mold growth, and costly repairs over time.

There are two primary approaches to waterproofing: interior and exterior systems. Interior waterproofing focuses on managing water that has already entered the basement, typically using drainage systems, sump pumps, and sealants. Exterior waterproofing, on the other hand, prevents water from penetrating the foundation in the first place. This method often involves excavating around the home, applying waterproof membranes, and installing proper drainage solutions. In a city like Toronto, where weather conditions can be unpredictable, many homeowners choose a combination of both methods for maximum protection.

Professional waterproofing services also include foundation crack repair, weeping tile installation, and moisture control systems. Addressing small issues early can prevent larger structural problems and protect indoor air quality. Mold and mildew thrive in damp environments, making waterproofing not just a structural concern but also a health priority. Experienced contractors assess each property individually, taking into account soil conditions, grading, and the age of the building.

Investing in waterproofing is a long-term solution that enhances property value and peace of mind. For homeowners in Toronto, it’s not just about fixing current leaks—it’s about preventing future damage and ensuring a dry, safe living space year-round. Whether building a new home or maintaining an older property, proper waterproofing is a crucial step in protecting your investment.

Sometimes in life, the biggest efforts are the ones no one talks about. They happen quietly, inside homes, inside daily routines, inside ordinary moments. For a long time, I never really thought about it. Life was just moving normally, and I assumed everything worked that way naturally.
But one day something small happened that changed the way I see everyday life.
I remember when I was younger, I would wake up in the morning and everything was already ready. Breakfast was on the table, my clothes were washed, the house looked clean, and everything felt normal. As a child I never stopped to think how all of this actually happened. It just felt like part of life.
One day I woke up very early, earlier than usual. The house was quiet. Outside the sun was just starting to rise. I walked into the kitchen and saw someone already working there, preparing things for the day. It was not something special, just normal daily work. But for the first time I realized that this “normal” routine actually takes effort.
Real effort.
From that day, I slowly started noticing many small things that I had ignored before.
For example, when guests come to the house, people only see the clean rooms, the prepared food, and the smiling faces. But they don’t see the hours of preparation before that moment. They don’t see the planning, the cleaning, the cooking, and the small worries that everything should go well.
Another example I noticed in daily life is when someone in the family gets sick. Suddenly the house changes rhythm. Someone starts paying extra attention, making sure medicines are taken, food is prepared properly, and everyone else in the house continues their normal routine. Most of the time, people only remember the person who was sick, but rarely the person who quietly managed everything around them.
I also remember a time when our family was going through a stressful period. Everyone was worried about different things. At that time I noticed how someone in the house kept trying to maintain peace. Even when feeling tired, they still spoke calmly, still helped others, still tried to keep the home environment stable.
Those efforts were never announced.
No one said, “Look how much work this takes.”
But those efforts held the family together.
Another thing I realized is that appreciation often comes very late. Sometimes years later we suddenly remember small things from our childhood. We remember who woke up early for us, who waited late at night, who kept things organized even when life was difficult.
And then we think… we never really said thank you.
Now when I look at everyday life, I try to notice these quiet efforts more carefully. They may not appear on social media, they may not become big achievements, and people rarely celebrate them.
But honestly, many homes, many families, and many peaceful lives exist because of these unnoticed efforts.
Sometimes the strongest contributions in life are not loud, not visible, and not rewarded.
They are simply done out of care.
And maybe the least we can do is learn to notice them. 🌿
result.title: The Day I Realized How Much Effort Goes Unnoticed

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPs3Nbsmf4iHXCFPQaKepsTWXKN6P7yjKsweyoSjff7Fz/1776326450666.jpg)


***
***
Today I went for a walk with no set direction, just wanting to get lost for a while among the wild vegetation of my Cuba, and let me tell you, the tropics can give you shows that even the best theater in the world cannot match.
***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaox483ZC2Jc36XcWvCWzfwEHrvFikyjdrsikrse6VmHo/1776326451656.jpg)
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZo65uNkPbQSiiDjAaSyVcTPwy8Q8QjrrQBAuno354Ex4/1776326597649.jpg)


***
The path I chose was one of those that smell of wet earth and sun. On both sides, the undergrowth spilled over with that messy joy that only plants growing freely, with no one to set limits for them, possess. There were weeds brushing against my knees, bushes that seemed to want to whisper secrets in my ear, while the air smelled of brand new greenery.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaBoPi7gJu9rnpkTNKMH12EBqhgkfQG8wZzwSG52THh5Q/1776326561173.jpg)
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYjvhyUkspB1skFsppj7L44LJVyb8kfKYHtAS3hKXTrCa/1776326597244.jpg)

***
Then, without warning, I saw them. At first they were just tiny pink flashes among all that green, but as I advanced, those flashes became patches, and the patches became whole blankets falling from tree branches, as if someone had poured living paint from above. They were vines, I discovered as I got closer. They were delicate but bold, climbing up trunks, hanging down like curtains, carpeting the grass, and tangling themselves around the stems of other plants with a familiarity that made me envious.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdeHKCPg5ZfkgfArvJsYizzyh5vjHzbLPromHw93VE5Ee/1776326560515.jpg)
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYRcVwiLHWeR3mEig22aWiXineALH5xXYVQYC8D1WAw8B/1776326452404.jpg)

***
The flowers were very tiny, but so abundant that they seemed like thousands of pink eyes looking at me from everywhere. A vibrant pink, the kind that cheers your retina just by resting your eyes on it. I have no idea what they are called, but that did not stop me from staying there, hypnotized, as if I had found a buried treasure.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQme6bfVqH1ZhYx6VRUcGhd6orG2ZszRu461GZ5t9jqvtSy/1776326560786.jpg)
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTjeTkvqdJ2mYC8PsQQ4ejDcVWFhXZFeBQ4kYjNrwBWSm/1776326452081.jpg)

***
The most beautiful thing, however, was not just the color, but the buzz. Where there were flowers, there were bees buzzing back and forth with that happy hurry they have when the nectar is good and the sun is shining. It looked like a small airport of winged creatures, all obsessed with those pink petals, and there I was in the middle, feeling privileged to witness something so simple and so perfect: life that happens without asking permission, and beauty that needs no sign or ticket.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmThLzHqRpepKrUXpSB96KydfbYZ1g1kMhHD5UF3AfkttL/1776326561671.jpg)

***
I sat on the grass for a good while, just looking, and I thought that sometimes the tropics remind you why they are unique. You do not need to go far, you do not need to look for postcard landscapes. It is enough to walk slowly along any path, with a clear gaze, and let the wild vegetation give you a lesson in humility and beauty.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZvYb7GiwLdDUJxyqCXE1jmiz1rkJ7SFrMtBm3mhJTacY/1776326561483.jpg)

***
So today I fell in love with some pink flowers that grow tangled around everything they can grab, without knowing their name, but indeed knowing how they made me feel: light, grateful, and alive.

### <center>VERSIÓN EN ESPAÑOL</center>

![cinti 800x20 - copia.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWKGeMBmj14VqKn8xBrmpFM3RYVcgmAXX6bGnGwuNWEnc/cinti%20800x20%20-%20copia.jpg) 

## <center> Cuando unas enredaderas rosadas me robaron el alma</center>



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcMr17XTvCzFLPZhLUhA7v5BSj8sSHPexGbnWhAb4LuQF/1776326451045.jpg)



***
***
Hoy salí a caminar sin rumbo fijo, solo con las ganas de perderme un rato entre la vegetación salvaje de mi Cuba y déjenme decirles que el trópico les puede regalar espectáculos que ni el mejor teatro del mundo puede igualar.
***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaox483ZC2Jc36XcWvCWzfwEHrvFikyjdrsikrse6VmHo/1776326451656.jpg)
***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZo65uNkPbQSiiDjAaSyVcTPwy8Q8QjrrQBAuno354Ex4/1776326597649.jpg)


***
El camino que elegí era de esos que huelen a tierra mojada y a sol. A ambos lados, la maleza se desbordaba con esa alegría desordenada que solo tienen las plantas que crecen libres, sin nadie que les ponga límites. Se podían ver hierbas que me rozaban las rodillas, arbustos que parecían querer contarme secretos al oído, mientras que el aire olía a verde recién estrenado.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaBoPi7gJu9rnpkTNKMH12EBqhgkfQG8wZzwSG52THh5Q/1776326561173.jpg)
***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYjvhyUkspB1skFsppj7L44LJVyb8kfKYHtAS3hKXTrCa/1776326597244.jpg)


***
Entonces, sin avisar, las vi. Al principio fueron solo pequeños destellos rosados entre tanto verde, pero conforme avanzaba, esos destellos se fueron haciendo manchas, y las manchas, mantos enteros que caían desde las ramas de los árboles como si alguien hubiera derramado pintura viva desde lo alto. Eran enredaderas, descubrí al acercarme. Eran delicadas pero atrevidas, que trepaban por los troncos, se descolgaban como cortinas, alfombraban el pasto y se enredaban en los tallos de otras plantas con una familiaridad que daba envidia.
***



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdeHKCPg5ZfkgfArvJsYizzyh5vjHzbLPromHw93VE5Ee/1776326560515.jpg)
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYRcVwiLHWeR3mEig22aWiXineALH5xXYVQYC8D1WAw8B/1776326452404.jpg)

***
Las flores eran pequeñísimas, pero tan abundantes que parecían miles de ojos rosados mirándome desde todas partes. Un rosa vibrante, de esos que te alegran la retina solo con posar la vista encima. No tengo ni idea de cómo se llaman, pero eso no me impidió quedarme allí, hipnotizada, como si hubiera encontrado un tesoro enterrado.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQme6bfVqH1ZhYx6VRUcGhd6orG2ZszRu461GZ5t9jqvtSy/1776326560786.jpg)
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTjeTkvqdJ2mYC8PsQQ4ejDcVWFhXZFeBQ4kYjNrwBWSm/1776326452081.jpg)

***
Lo más bonito, sin embargo, no era solo el color, era el bullicio, porque donde había flores, había abejas zumbando de un lado a otro con esa prisa feliz que tienen cuando el néctar es bueno y el sol acompaña. Parecía un pequeño aeropuerto de criaturas aladas, todas obsesionadas con esos pétalos rosados, y yo allí, en medio, sintiéndome privilegiada por ser testigo de algo tan sencillo y tan perfecto: la vida que se da sin pedir permiso y la belleza que no necesita cartel ni entrada.
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmThLzHqRpepKrUXpSB96KydfbYZ1g1kMhHD5UF3AfkttL/1776326561671.jpg)


***
Me quedé un buen rato sentada en el pasto, solo mirando, y pensé que a veces el trópico te recuerda por qué es único. No hace falta irse lejos, no hace falta buscar paisajes postales. Basta con caminar despacio por un camino cualquiera, con la mirada limpia, y dejar que la vegetación silvestre te regale una lección de humildad y de belleza.
***



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZvYb7GiwLdDUJxyqCXE1jmiz1rkJ7SFrMtBm3mhJTacY/1776326561483.jpg)

***
Así que hoy me enamoré de unas flores rosas que crecen enredadas en todo lo que pillan, sin saber su nombre, pero sí sabiendo cómo me hicieron sentir: liviana, agradecida y viva.

<center>🌸</center>
<center>🌸</center>

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRSmczRZ7mh457ozsGyfJF93vxnsidtnD9LmCYpF1XK9K/1775880207279.jpg)

<sub>🍃 **¡𝑮𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒊𝒂𝒔 𝒑𝒐𝒓 𝒍𝒆𝒆𝒓!** 🍃
𝑺𝒊 𝒂ú𝒏 𝒏𝒐 𝒎𝒆 𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒐𝒄𝒆𝒔: 𝒔𝒐𝒚 **𝒏𝒆𝒖𝒓ó𝒍𝒐𝒈𝒂 𝒚 𝒆𝒔𝒄𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒐𝒓𝒂 𝒄𝒖𝒃𝒂𝒏𝒂**, 𝒎𝒂𝒅𝒓𝒆, 𝒎𝒖𝒋𝒆𝒓 𝒚 𝒔𝒐ñ𝒂𝒅𝒐𝒓𝒂 𝒒𝒖𝒆 𝒆𝒏𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒕𝒓ó 𝒆𝒏 𝑯𝒊𝒗𝒆 𝒖𝒏 𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒎𝒐𝒔𝒐 𝒆𝒔𝒑𝒂𝒄𝒊𝒐 𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂 𝒗𝒐𝒍𝒂𝒓.  
**𝑬𝒍 𝒕𝒆𝒙𝒕𝒐 𝒚 𝒍𝒂𝒔 𝒊𝒎á𝒈𝒆𝒏𝒆𝒔 𝒔𝒐𝒏 𝒅𝒆 𝒎𝒊 𝒂𝒖𝒕𝒐𝒓í𝒂**, 100% 𝒉𝒖𝒎𝒂𝒏𝒐𝒔 (𝒔𝒊𝒏 𝑰𝑨).  
𝑩𝒂𝒏𝒏𝒆𝒓 𝒅𝒊𝒔𝒆ñ𝒂𝒅𝒐 𝒑𝒐𝒓 𝑳𝒖𝒎𝒊𝒊.
¿𝑻𝒆 𝒈𝒖𝒔𝒕ó 𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒂 𝒑𝒖𝒃𝒍𝒊𝒄𝒂𝒄𝒊ó𝒏? **𝑽𝒐𝒕𝒂, 𝒄𝒐𝒎𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒂 𝒐 𝒓𝒆𝒃𝒍𝒐𝒈𝒖𝒆𝒂** 𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂 𝒂𝒚𝒖𝒅𝒂𝒓 𝒂 𝒅𝒆𝒔𝒑𝒍𝒆𝒈𝒂𝒓 𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒔 𝒂𝒍𝒂𝒔. 💗</sub>

‎<div class="text-justify"> Animals are rich in immense love. Especially in this unique diversity of rural Bengal full of greenery. And in this green space, goats are living a free life and spending time happily with the green grass. They have happily jumped and eaten leaves. I will tell you about the beautiful view of such green nature and the free roaming of animals.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRfmbtC451Kj7oxuhxVftrruKo3RQjsUZ4HWSMDXh7FvW/1774236020492.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXCDRU2uLhaxDtj2jqS3F7hwZ1x4vGVBdyYzAU4MbL9fm/1774236020660.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbtbERCMZ79JDcTNt32vjeQk7cbDVbvycS4vhBS9CwkcS/1774236020815.jpg)

The beautiful view of the green grass below gives a sense of tranquility to the mind. The sweet smell of the earth along with the green grass creates a captivating attraction. The people of rural Bengal do not raise goats with joy. Even though there are no paddy fields or crops here, they are openly enjoying eating the leaves here. They are living a free and beautiful life in such an environment. I am really happy and pleased to see such a free life of animals. Do you also like this beautiful free life? Then come to this green vine. Where your breathing is normal and you can also join yourself in this beautiful life.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfZAKRhYRRN7nAJQ9v5kbiALz5UD2hPKMXhsyi4r7VUfH/1774236020960.jpg)

But there was a severe storm at night. So this unique green grass of nature seems to be smiling. It seems to be deeper than green or green like an island. The animals are feeling a slight chill in the dry environment. And are enjoying the joy of eating grass openly. Such a beautiful environment always gives me the opportunity to enjoy this green forest. Cycas is a tree where animals wait to rest. The leaves and branches of this tree are very interesting to see.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPsKXuR3KS6pDqvJp8QPan8so9oMF7bLRhaTCqWvd1CbN/1774236021118.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXhWz25knVU4BfTpxTkz3WzHSESaRczMBCT6LqJRn25qw/1774236117875.jpg)

They are trying to walk on long legs in this beautiful green wilderness. And they are enjoying the pleasure of choosing big grass from small grasses. Ah, how keenly they are trying to see. I welcome you all to this free lifestyle of animals. Along with this, there is also an opportunity to earn a living by raising goats in a rural environment. So, we can make ourselves self-reliant by raising animals. Let us value time and include ourselves in livelihood.
